courses.title: Business and Technical Writing
courses.description: Study and practice of presenting technical information, with emphasis on formal and informal writing for the workplace, including resumes, job application letters, instructions, proposals, and reports.
courses.prerequisiteText: 010 core complete and 040 core complete

courses.title: Medical Writing
courses.description: The study and practice of interpreting and incorporating findings and statistical results into clear, comprehensible and well-organized prose.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: Proposal Writing
courses.description: Practice in writing and editing a series of proposals of varying scope and complexity.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: Environmental Writing
courses.description: Practice in presenting information about environmental issues as addressed by government, industry, private organizations and the mass media.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: Science Writing
courses.description: The study and practice of documenting, reporting and presenting science in articles, audiovisual scripts, specifications, reports and proposals.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: General Biology I
courses.description: A survey of current biological concepts for students majoring in the sciences. Emphasis will be placed on biological molecules, cellular metabolism, cell division, heredity and the regulation of genes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 1101, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete) and MATH 1301.

prerequisites.text: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 1101, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete) and MATH 1301.

courses.title: General Biology Laboratory I
courses.description: Appropriate exercises and experiments requiring scientific observation and analysis that illustrate some of the basic techniques, concepts and facts presented in BIOL 1301. (BIOL 1106)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 1301.

courses.title: General Biology II
courses.description: A survey of current biological concepts for students majoring in the sciences. Emphasis will be placed on topics which include evolution, biological diversity, ecology, and comparative structure and function of organ systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1101, BIOL 1301 and enrollment in BIOL 1102.

courses.title: General Biology Laboratory II
courses.description: Appropriate exercises and experiments requiring scientific observation and analysis that illustrate some of the basic techniques, concepts and facts presented in BIOL 1302. (BIOL 1107)
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1101 and credit or enrollment in BIOL 1302.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: The first in a two course survey of the fundamentals of general chemistry for students majoring in the sciences. Descriptive material is correlated with the basic chemical principles and their applications. Modern concepts of atomic and molecular structure, chemical bonding, the gaseous state and the kinetic molecular theory of matter will be analyzed. There will be on stoichiometeric calculations of mass and molar relationships, energy relations and intermolecular forces.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1301 and CHEM 1107, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete), and one year of high school chemistry or CHEM 1305/CHEM 1105.

prerequisites.text: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1301 and CHEM 1107, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete), and one year of high school chemistry or CHEM 1305/CHEM 1105.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Experiments which illustrate basic laboratory techniques and procedures, physical and chemical properties, stoichiometry, solutions, and thermochemistry. (CHEM 1111)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 1307.

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: The second in a two course survey of the fundamentals of general chemistry for students majoring in the sciences. Topics include liquids and solids, intermolecular forces, chemical kinetics, thermodynamics, homogeneous, heterogeneous and ionic equilibrium, modern concepts of acids and bases, electrochemistry, coordination chemistry, nuclear chemistry and selected topics.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in CHEM 1307 and credit or enrollment in CHEM 1108.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: Emphasis on reactions in aqueous solutions, gas laws, equilibrium, kinetics and qualitative analysis, with an introduction to instrumental analysis. (CHEM 1112)
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 1107 and credit or enrollment in CHEM 1308.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: This course will cover various types of organic compounds, their classification, structure, naming, chemical and physical properties, reactivity, preparation, and techniques to identify them.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in CHEM 1308 and CHEM 1108. Enrollment in CHEM 2101 is recommended.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments illustrating basic techniques, synthesis, interpretation of spectra, use of molecular models and scientific literature.
courses.prerequisiteText: A letter grade of C or better in CHEM 2301 or enrollment in CHEM 2301.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: This course will cover the nomenclature, preparation, reactions, reaction mechanisms, and spectroscopy of alkenes, alkynes, aromatic compounds, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids and derivatives, and amines.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisites/ corequisites: A letter grade of C or better in CHEM 2301 and CHEM 2101. Enrollment in CHEM 2102 is recommended.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisites/ corequisites: A letter grade of C or better in CHEM 2301 and CHEM 2101. Enrollment in CHEM 2102 is recommended.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II Laboratory
courses.description: This course covers the experiments illustrating multistep synthesis, semi micro techniques, instrumental analysis, and qualitative analysis.
courses.prerequisiteText: A letter grade of C or better in CHEM 2302 or enrollment in CHEM 2302.

courses.title: General Physics I
courses.description: This is the first in a two-part survey of general physics for science majors focusing on elementary principles of mechanics, heat and wave motion using elementary trigonometry and algebra. Topics include kinematics, dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; conservation of mass, momentum and energy; simple harmonic motion and characteristics of waves, mechanical and thermal properties of solids and fluids; and thermal properties, kinetics and dynamics of ideal gases. Credit for both PHYS 1307 and PHYS 2401 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1302 or the equivalent, enrollment in PHYS 1107.

courses.title: General Physics Laboratory I
courses.description: Topics include mechanics, bulk properties of matter, heat and waves. (PHYS 1101)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 1307.

courses.title: Physics I
courses.description: This is the first in a two-part survey of physics for science majors using calculus. Topics include kinematics and dynamics in one, two and three dimensions, statics, dynamics, potentials, conservation of energy and momentum (linear and angular), rotational kinematics and dynamics, oscillations, gravitation, fluid mechanics, thermal properties of matter, kinetic theory of gases and the first and second law of thermodynamics. Credit for both PHYS 1307 and PHYS 2401 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit in MATH 2402 (or MATH 2412) enrollment in PHYS 2101.

courses.title: Physics Laboratory I
courses.description: Topics include linear and rotational motion, collisions, simple harmonic motion and thermal properties of matter. (PHYS 2125)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 2401.

courses.title: General Physics II
courses.description: This is the second in a two-part survey of general physics for science majors focusing on elementary principles of electromagnetism, optics and modern physics using elementary trigonometry and algebra. Topics include static electric and magnetic fields and the motion of charged particles therein; induced electric and magnetic fields; DC and AC circuits; geometrical and physical optics; the concept of quantization and the properties of the atom and its nucleus. Credit for both PHYS 1308 and PHYS 2402 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHYS 1307 and credit or enrollment in PHYS 1108.

courses.title: General Physics Laboratory II
courses.description: Topics include electric and magnetic fields, DC and AC circuits, non-linear devices, geometric and physical optics, and atomic and molecular physics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 1308.

courses.title: Physics II
courses.description: This is the second in a two-part survey of physics for science majors using calculus. Topics include electric charge, electric fields and potentials, Gauss’ Law, capacitors and dielectrics, AC and DC electrical circuits, magnetic fields, the Biot-Savart Law, Faraday’s Law, magnetic properties of matter, Maxwell’s equations and electromagnetic waves and optics. Credit for both PHYS 1308 and PHYS 2402 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: Grade of C or better in PHYS 2401 and credit or enrollment in PHYS 2102.

courses.title: Physics Laboratory II
courses.description: Topics include static electric and magnetic fields and electron motion therein, DC and AC circuits including linear and nonlinear devices and properties of electromagnetic waves, and geometrical and physical optics. (PHYS 2126)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 2402.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: Independent investigation of a specific topic or problem in chemistry research under the direction of a selected faculty member.
courses.prerequisiteText: Approval by the Natural Sciences Department, minimum GPA of 2.0, and permission of instructor.

items.text: Approval by the Natural Sciences Department

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
courses.description: A study of chemical equilibrium, reliability of measurements and the theory of applications of gravimetric, volumetric and instrumental methods of analysis.
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 1308 and CHEM 1108 and credit or enrollment in CHEM 3110.

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Quantitative methods of analysis including gravimetric, volumetric and instrumental. Instrumental methods will include absorption and emission spectroscopy, gas and liquid chromatography and electrochemical analysis.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 3310.

courses.title: Environmental Chemistry
courses.description: Chemistry and analysis of clean and polluted air and water. Environmental standards of the American Public Health Association and the US Environmental Protection Agency.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302 and BIOL 1102; and CHEM 1308 and CHEM 1108.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry I
courses.description: Study and applications of the first and second laws of thermodynamics to gases, liquids, solutions and phase equilibrium; applications of the third law of thermodynamics to systems in equilibrium; kinetic theory and statistical thermodynamics.
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 2301/CHEM 2101, MATH 2402, one year of general physics, and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 3130.

prerequisites.text: CHEM 2301/CHEM 2101, MATH 2402, one year of general physics, and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 3130.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Advanced experiments in physical chemistry including studies in thermodynamics, colligative properties of solutions, surface tension of surfactant containing solutions, solution viscosities, electrochemistry and the physical chemistry of polymeric materials. In addition to providing support for CHEM 3330, this course is designed to acquaint the student with the experimental approaches and laboratory techniques used in industrial research and development activities.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit for or enrollment in CHEM 3330.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry II
courses.description: Study and applications of the fundamental principles and postulates of quantum mechanics, electronic structure of atoms and molecules, molecular symmetry, and spectroscopy.
courses.prerequisiteText: (1) CHEM 3330 and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 3132 OR (2) CHEM 2301/CHEM 2101, MATH 2402, one year of general physics, and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 3132.

prerequisites.text: (1) CHEM 3330 and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 3132 OR (2) CHEM 2301/CHEM 2101, MATH 2402, one year of general physics, and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 3132.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: A continuation of CHEM 3130.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit for or enrollment in CHEM 3332.

courses.title: Instrumental Methods of Analysis
courses.description: Theory and operation of advanced measurement sciences, especially modern atomic/molecular spectroscopy, electrochemical analysis, and separation. Major instrumentation will be learned in experimental contexts, including signal processing, AA, ICP, fluorescence, UV-VIS, IR, NMR, voltammetry, ion-selective sensor, HPLC, and GC/MS.
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 3310/CHEM 3110

courses.title: General Biochemistry I
courses.description: Overview of fundamental biochemical principles, topics, techniques and analytical methods that integrates concepts from previous biology and chemistry courses to the study of biological macromolecules. Emphasis is placed on the bioorganic chemistry and techniques needed to critically and objectively analyze biological molecules and the fundamental processes that support life. Specifically protein, lipid and membrane structure and function, enzymatic catalysis and kinetics are emphasized.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1102 and BIOL 1302 and CHEM 2101 and CHEM 2301.

courses.title: General Biochemistry Lab I
courses.description: Experiments in biochemistry to accompany CHEM 4340.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 4340.

courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: An introduction to modern inorganic chemistry including theoretical and descriptive chemistry, along with discussion of important applications. The theoretical aspects include the quantum mechanical basis of atomic and molecular structure, the nature of chemical bonding, and the thermodynamics and kinetics of inorganic reactions. The descriptive component involves the application of the theoretical principles to the actual properties of the elements and their respective compounds. The course also includes a discussion of some of the most important scientific, technological, and industrial applications of inorganic chemistry.
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 3330 /CHEM 3130 and CHEM 3332/CHEM 3132 and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 4162.

prerequisites.text: CHEM 3330 /CHEM 3130 and CHEM 3332/CHEM 3132 and credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 4162.

courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory course is designed to supplement CHEM 4362. It will involve experiments that demonstrate the principles of inorganic chemistry and the techniques used by inorganic chemists for the synthesis and characterization of inorganic materials.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 4362.

courses.title: Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: A study of the chemistry and technology of polymeric materials including methods of polymerization, characterization and applications of polymers with an emphasis on chemistry, structure-property relationships, and polymer processing methods.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit for CHEM 2301/CHEM 2101. Corequisite(s): CHEM 4164

courses.title: Polymer Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: This course covers the chemistry and technology of polymeric materials in a laboratory, including methods of polymerization, characterization and applications of polymers. A link with end use products of polymers and structure of known polymers will be examined. Additionally, recyclability of different polymer compositions will be demonstrated in the laboratory. This lab is intended to supplement the concepts learned in the CHEM 4364 polymer chemistry class.
courses.prerequisiteText: Corequisite(s): CHEM 4364

courses.title: Introductory Chemistry
courses.description: A survey of chemistry which focuses on the composition, properties and interaction of substances necessary to produce new materials. Topics include stoichiometry, atomic structure, chemical bonds, states of matter, electrolyte solutions and chemical reactions. This course is required for nursing or similar professional programs and may be taken prior to the general chemistry courses for science majors.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 1105 and credit or enrollment in MATH 1301 or MATH 1310

prerequisites.text: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 1105 and credit or enrollment in MATH 1301 or MATH 1310

courses.title: Introductory Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Appropriate laboratory experiments for the student who will not be a professional physical scientist. The experiments support the principles of chemistry developed in the lecture portion of the course and illustrate some of the basic approaches to chemical problems. (CHEM 1105)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 1305.

courses.title: Contemporary Mathematics
courses.description: An introduction to contemporary mathematical ideas and problem-solving techniques. Designed for students requiring one college-level mathematics course. This course cannot be applied toward any degree in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics or the Department of Computer Science and Engineering Technology (MATH 1332)
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MATH 0300, or TSIA2 score meeting college readiness in Mathematics, or TSIA2 MATH complete, or TSIA2 MATH exempt. For current TSIA2 College Readiness scores, please see https://www.uhd.edu/testing/Pages/testing-tsia.aspx.

items.text: TSIA2 score meeting college readiness in Mathematics

courses.title: Beginning Algebra
courses.description: This course is intended to build and reinforce the essential geometry, arithmetic and algebra skills needed for MATH 1300 - Intermediate Algebra. Topics include real numbers and their properties, order of operations and simplifying real-valued expressions, simplifying algebraic expressions, solving linear equations and inequalities, solving systems of equations in two variables, an introduction to the Cartesian coordinate system and word problems. This course may not be used to satisfy degree requirements.
courses.prerequisiteText: A TSIA2 score that does not meet college readiness in Mathematics, and co-enrollment in MATH 1310 or STAT 1312. Successful completion of MATH 1310 or STAT 1312 (with a C or better) will satisfy the TSI requirements for developmental mathematics. For current TSIA2 College Readiness scores, please see https://www.uhd.edu/testing/Pages/testing-tsia.aspx

courses.title: Statistical Literacy
courses.description: An introduction to statistical ideas and statistical reasoning, and their relevance to modern life. STAT 1312 is designed for students requiring one college-level mathematics course. This course cannot be applied toward any degree in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MATH 0300, or TSIA2 score meeting college readiness in Mathematics, or TSIA2 MATH complete, or TSIA2 MATH exempt. For current TSIA2 College Readiness scores, please see https://www.uhd.edu/testing/Pages/testing-tsia.aspx.
